description: We are a team of students from the Faculty of Computers and Data Science at Alexandria University, passionate about AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Data Science.  We are have with skills in AI/ML, Data Science, Software Development and Problem Solving. We value teamwork, creativity, and turning ideas into real-world solutions.
summary: ignite is the team responsible of the flame in free fall project and we solved it using AI powered dashboards that let us combine and make relationships between existing researches that research various topics that help us in this project
details: Ignite is a web application that helps people planning crewed space missions understand how fire behaves in space. We structured 24 NASA microgravity combustion investigations from the Physical Sciences Informatics database into one dataset, then built three tools on it. The fire dashboard lets a user enter a crew environment, including oxygen level, pressure, airflow, material, diluent and gravity, and compares it with the conditions each investigation tested. It returns a flammability indicator, the factors behind it and the closest matching experiments, and a 3D flame changes shape with gravity. The research explorer shows how investigations connect through shared hardware, fuel and dependencies, with filters, detail cards and a side by side comparison. The AI assistant searches the research documents, answers with citations to the PSI report it used, and declines questions outside this topic. The main benefit is speed and trust, because engineers, researchers and students can find and compare relevant experiments in minutes and check every claim against its source. We hope to make decades of public NASA data useful for choosing materials and atmospheres for Moon bases, rovers and spacecraft, where cabins may run near 30 percent oxygen and 10.2 psi, and to reveal gaps such as the lack of partial gravity combustion data so future experiments can target them. We built the frontend with HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript, Tailwind, Three.js and a custom SVG graph. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, an MCP server that exposes research tools, BM25 search with query decomposition and rank fusion, and a language model through OpenRouter. We tested with pytest, worked with Git and GitHub, and everything runs on ordinary laptops without a GPU. The project is creative because the flame shape makes the effect of gravity visible, the assistant chooses by itself when to search and cites only what it found, and it answers in Arabic or English while searching English documents. Our team also weighed scientific honesty, so missing values are never guessed, the indicator is labeled as data matched and not a physics simulation, rocket propellant combustion is out of scope, and the API key stays on the server.
